shown_on_screen: New bill shown per option: 'Current bill Rs 100 -> new bill Rs {100+error}'. Frame the regime as possibly inaccurate so a higher bill reads as a POSSIBLE over-assessment (this framing is what keeps the corrective-vs-cheating distinction alive; pilot it).
description: Signed assessment error, % of liability. + = OVER-assessed (bill too high), - = under-assessed. The SINGLE consequence variable: it is the money channel (enters utility via the -1 numeraire through the new bill) AND supplies the over-assessment share that m1 keys off. Drawn on a discrete grid (gran 5), orthogonally to bribe. No separate beta is estimated for it. Replaces the old accuracy + measurement_error pair.

shown_on_screen: 'Informal payment (chai-pani): Rs Z' on Human options; 'Rs 0' on Satellite. New bill after deal = (100+error) - K*Z. Front-end must show NO bribe line on Satellite.
description: Informal payment, % of own liability. Human-only (forced 0 under Satellite). Discrete grid INCLUDING 0 (a clean inspector), which breaks the m/beta_satellite collinearity. No own beta: its cash effect enters money out of pocket as net = (1-K)*bribe; the MORAL cost of bribing is carried by m0/m1. theta_mean/theta_sd unused.

shown_on_screen: Option header: 'An inspector visits & measures' (Human) vs 'A satellite checks automatically' (Satellite).
description: Assessor type as an estimable MAIN EFFECT (money / %-of-liability units). beta_satellite > 0 => intrinsic preference for the satellite holding money fixed; ~0 => assessor matters only by gating the bribe. Categorical [Human, Satellite]; bribe forced 0 under Satellite. range_* are placeholders; prior read from theta_mean/theta_sd.

shown_on_screen: Not shown directly; revealed by refusing a money-saving bribe when the bill is FAIR (error <= 0).
description: Moral cost of bribing when the bill was FAIR (no over-assessment), % of liability. Sign free: m0>0 = averse (forgoes savings to stay clean = moral), m0~0 = indifferent, m0<0 = taste for the corrupt route. This is the clean real-morality number. Prior centred at 0; recalibrate after pilot.

shown_on_screen: Not shown directly; revealed by bribing MORE readily when the bill was over-assessed than when it was fair.
description: Erosion of the moral cost at FULL over-assessment, % of liability. moral_cost = m0 - m1 * (over_share in [0,1]). m1>0 (expected): each unit of over-assessment makes bribing feel more justified ('I'm owed it'). Low m0 = rent-seeker; high m0 + high m1 = corrector; high m0 + low m1 = rigidly honest. m1 is the regressive-corruptibility handle to regress on literacy / title / value-band.
